 Shelton pushes back: “It’s unfair to say this about Alcaraz and Sinner”
 October 27, 2026 06:00 PM by Antonio Frappola Add as preferred source on Google SHARE © ATP Tour Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner have both been forced to spend around four and a half months on the sidelines during an unfortunate 2026 season.
 ADVERTISEMENT
 Alcaraz began the year by becoming the youngest player to complete the Career Grand Slam, winning the Australian Open , before also triumphing in Doha. He suffered a wrist injury in Barcelona that kept him out of action until the US Open .
 Sinner, meanwhile, produced an extraordinary run by winning the first five Masters 1000 tournaments of the year, from Indian Wells to Rome, and successfully defended his title at Wimbledon . It was shortly after the Championships final, which he won in four sets against Alexander Zverev , that the Italian saw his right-knee problem worsen over the following weeks. He missed the entire American swing hoping to return to action in Europe, but things did not go according to plan and he ultimately set his sights on 2027.
 Shelton on Alcaraz and Sinner: “Their dominance...”
 On the eve of his debut in Basel, Ben Shelton was asked about the Tour’s two leading players.
 ADVERTISEMENT
 “Has Alcaraz and Sinner’s dominance diminished? They have won two of the four Grand Slam tournaments played this year, and Sinner has also claimed five Masters 1000 titles. I’m not sure to what extent you can say that their dominance has diminished,” the American said.
 “I think both of them will be in excellent shape heading into the 2027 Australian Open. It has been a shame for tennis that Carlos and Jannik have been unable to compete for a significant part of the season. Honestly, I would never go as far as saying that their dominance is coming to an end.
 “It is true that more and more young players are competing for the biggest titles and continuing to develop, but saying that Alcaraz and Sinner are losing their supremacy seems unfair to me.”
